stem.text: A powder is known to be either a single sodium halide or a mixture of two sodium halides. A sample of the powder was dissolved in water.
Aqueous silver nitrate was added, and a pale yellow precipitate was formed. When concentrated aqueous ammonia was then added, this precipitate partly dissolved leaving a darker yellow precipitate.

C.text: a mixture of sodium chloride and sodium bromide

D.text: a mixture of sodium chloride and sodium iodide
